# k0rdent_cluster_type_versions (Data Source)

Every version of one ClusterType, oldest first.

This is the nearest thing the platform has to a catalogue of supported Kubernetes versions. A tenant does not choose a Kubernetes version directly: it comes with the ClusterType version a cluster is bound to, so the list to read is this one.

Each entry's `self_link` is version-scoped, which is what pins a cluster to an immutable version instead of to whatever the latest one becomes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The Kubernetes versions a ClusterType offers. You get a Kubernetes version by
# picking a ClusterType version.
data "k0rdent_cluster_type_versions" "training" {
  cluster_type = "gpu-training"
  status       = "available"
}

# The list is oldest first, so reverse it and take the first for the newest.
locals {
  newest = reverse(data.k0rdent_cluster_type_versions.training.versions)[0]
}

output "kubernetes_versions" {
  value = distinct([for v in data.k0rdent_cluster_type_versions.training.versions : v.kubernetes_version])
}

# A version's `self_link` keeps the cluster on that version. The ClusterType's
# own `self_link` follows the newest.
resource "k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster" "pinned" {
  id           = "training-pinned"
  cluster_type = local.newest.self_link
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_type` (String) ClusterType slug whose history to read. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the versions whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. It runs before each kept version is read for its `kubernetes_version`, so a narrow pattern also saves those reads. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `status` (String) Return only versions with this lifecycle status: `draft`, `available` or `deprecated`. Omit it for all of them. Only `available` can back a new cluster. Filtered by the platform. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["draft" "available" "deprecated"].

### Read-Only

- `versions` (Attributes List) The history, oldest first. Sorted by `version`, then `version_id`. A new version appends, but a `status` filter shifts every index, so reach an entry with `for_each` over `version_id` rather than `versions[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--versions))

<a id="nestedatt--versions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `versions`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When this version was created, as RFC 3339. This is a row timestamp, not a support commitment: the platform publishes no end-of-support date for a version.
- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read, when one was set.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name, for display only.
- `kubernetes_version` (String) The k0s version this version of the type provisions, as `vX.Y.Z`. Null for a ClusterType that is not Kubernetes-flavoured. Two entries can carry the same one: a new ClusterType version may change node pools or CIDRs and leave Kubernetes where it was.
- `self_link` (String) Version-scoped reference, suitable for a cluster's `cluster_type`. Binds this exact version, so a new one being published does not move the cluster.
- `status` (String) `available`, `draft` or `deprecated`. The progression is forward-only and only `available` can back a new cluster.
- `version` (Number) Sequential version number, for display.
- `version_id` (String) UUID of this version. Stable, and what pins a reference.

## Related

- [`k0rdent_cluster_type_version`](../data-sources/cluster_type_version.md) data source: reads one by id.
- [`k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster`](../resources/kubernetes_cluster.md) resource: is pinned to a version by the version's `self_link`.
- [`k0rdent_cluster_type`](../data-sources/cluster_type.md) data source: reads the ClusterType at its newest version.
